KP 3. Finding the Slope of the Tangent Line to a Product at a Given Point
6.?
If a curve C is given by y=(x−1)ln⁡(2x+1), calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where x=0 is
−2
.
M
Wed, Jul 29th @ 7:02 PM|Elapsed: 2:56Correct

We differentiate using the product rule. Let u(x)=x−1 and v(x)=ln⁡(2x+1). Then, we have

dudx=1,dvdx=22x+1.

Applying the product rule gives

dydx=udvdx+vdudx=(x−1)⋅22x+1+ln⁡(2x+1)⋅1=2(x−1)2x+1+ln⁡(2x+1).

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute x=0 into the formula and get

dydx|x=0=2(0−1)2(0)+1+ln⁡(2(0)+1)=(−2)+ln⁡(1)=−2.

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is −2.

7.?

If a curve C is given by y=3x2tan⁡x, calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where x=π.

M
Wed, Jul 29th @ 7:06 PM|Elapsed: 3:42Correct

We differentiate using the product rule. Let u(x)=3x2 and v(x)=tan⁡x. Then, we have

dudx=6x,dvdx=sec2⁡x.

Applying the product rule gives

dydx=udvdx+vdudx=(3x2)(sec2⁡x)+(tan⁡x)(6x)=3x2sec2⁡x+6xtan⁡x.

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute x=π into the formula and get

dydx|x=π=3x2sec2⁡x+6xtan⁡x|x=π=3(π)2sec2⁡(π)+6(π)tan⁡(π)=3π2⋅1+6π⋅0=3π2.

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is 3π2.
